title: pv-dash standalone acl file — the write-registers gate
description: The standalone acl file the modbus-cache --write-registers file:<path> knob reads (cache/examples/acl-write-registers.json is the shipped example) — the same object a device profile carries under "acl"/"write": an optional terse-ASCII desc, the optional gate type naming the schema, and the ordered rules list. The chain reads top to bottom, the LAST matching rule decides, and a register no rule decides refuses (the default deny any). The register kind's matcher is the bare word any (all registers), ONE "START:COUNT" string, or a JSON array of those (the profile's multi-range form; a comma-joined string is NOT the register kind's list form); the loader bounds every range (count >= 1, start + count <= 65536 — the 16-bit space; the canonical spelling carries no leading zeros). A typeless register gate reads as write-registers (the legacy shape). The loader (cache/lib/config.py's _write_gate_object) stays the strict word (the exact bounds, the dead-rule linting lives in scripts/lint_acl.py); a group/world-readable acl file warns (chmod 0600 silences it).

desc.description: The gate's terse-ASCII description — the % line of the show write registers profile report.

type.description: The schema kind: range rules. Optional — a typeless register gate reads as write-registers (the legacy shape); a file spelling the ip-prefix type refuses this reader.

rules.description: The ordered rule chain: the clean-slate deny ("any"), the allows, the deny carves, the re-opens. A rule never the last match for any register is dead (scripts/lint_acl.py catches it).

type.description: The verdict this rule hands every register its matcher decides.

oneOf.description: any — every register in the 16-bit space.
One range START:COUNT (a bare IP-style single range; the loader bounds it).
The multi-range list form (the profile's shape); the word any stands alone, never inside a list.

range.description: The matcher: what this rule's verdict decides.

desc.description: The rule's terse-ASCII description — speaks for the whole matcher (a list's ranges share the one comment).
